summary: Iteration 5 (Vetaura BYOK + A2P 10DLC + Invitations + Overage billing + Discharge email) — FULL PASS after one server-side fix. Backend: 22/22 pytest in /app/backend/tests/test_iter5.py (~13s). Verified: (1) GET /api/integrations/twilio returns {connected: bool}; POST with format-valid but fake AC/SK/secret rejected with HTTP 400 'Twilio credentials invalid: ...'. Note: the exact literal request-spec payload 'ACfakefake...'/'SKfakefake...'/'fakefake' is rejected upstream by Pydantic (422) because 'fakefake' <10 chars and 'ACfake...' is non-hex — I changed my test to use 32-hex fakes with 12-char secret so it reaches the live Twilio API path which correctly 400s. (2) POST /api/integrations/email with bogus Resend key → 400. (3) GET /api/compliance/sms/profile lazy-seeds 11 checklist items + brand_status='not_started' + readiness{ready:false,state:'blocked',checklist_total:11}. (4) PATCH /profile persists brand/campaign/legal identity. (5) POST /consent + GET /consent list + POST /consent/opt-out + GET /consent/events all work — after I fixed one _id-serialisation bug (see below). (6) GET /preflight?phone=+15559998888&message_type=care → allowed:false with reason. (7) Tokenised Twilio SMS webhooks: seeded twilio_credentials (with proper Fernet-encrypted api_key_secret via crypto_service.encrypt) + twilio_numbers doc. STOP → TwiML with 'unsubscribed'; HELP → TwiML containing 'STOP'; 'my dog collapsed' (from same number after STOP) → TwiML with clinic name + STOP footer; wrong webhook_token → 'not configured' TwiML (no exception); consent_events for +15551234567 include (care,opt_out) AND (marketing,opt_out); care consent for that phone remains opted_out (auto-opt-in guard fires correctly). (8) Invitations: owner creates invite → returns {token, invite_url, delivered_by_email:false}; GET /api/invitations/{token} public peek returns email/role/clinic_name/invited_by; POST /api/auth/signup with invite_token attaches user to vet1's clinic with role=tech; new tech user CAN list team members, CANNOT create invites (403) or delete members (403). (9) Billing: GET /api/billing-cycle/preview (auth) returns dict; POST /close without X-Admin-Token → 403; with X-Admin-Token='admin-cron-secret-change-me' → {reported:[], count:N}. (10) Discharge email fallback: POST /discharge/email with nonexistent token → 404; POST /ai/discharge with email_to when no email provider connected → email_delivered:false, email_error:'email_not_configured'. Frontend: verified /app/integrations (Twilio card + Email provider card visible), /app/compliance (11 checklist items rendered as radio buttons — my initial `input[type=checkbox]` selector under-counted; UI actually renders them as custom radios but all 11 items ARE present with Brand+Campaign attestation cards, Business identity fields, and the amber legal-text warning), /app/team (Send invite form with Email/Role/Name inputs, Members list with roles, Pending invites list with copyable URLs), /app/phone (Twilio not-connected banner visible), /invite/{valid_token} (renders 'Join Meadow Ridge Vet on Vetaura', shows read-only email, name+password inputs, Accept invitation button), /invite/{bad_token} (shows error state), /app/discharges (loads with owner-email hint).

minor.issue: FIXED IN THIS RUN — routes returned the inserted doc which still had Mongo ObjectId `_id` after insert_one, causing FastAPI JSON serialisation to raise 500 ValueError. Fixed by adding `doc.pop('_id', None)` after `db.consent_events.insert_one(doc)` in sms_compliance.record_consent_transition. This is the same pattern that already exists elsewhere in the code.

action_items: auth.py SignupReq: `clinic_name: str = Field(min_length=1, default='')` — the default value fails min_length=1 validation, so any signup that omits clinic_name (or sends '') returns 422 Unprocessable Entity even when invite_token is provided. Change to `clinic_name: Optional[str] = None` (or drop the min_length constraint, since business rule 'clinic_name required unless invite_token' is enforced manually in the handler). Currently the invite-signup flow only works if the client sends a non-empty dummy clinic_name (frontend does this, so it works — but the API contract is footgun-y).

credentials_service.get_twilio_creds unconditionally calls crypto_service.decrypt() on the stored ciphertext; if the ciphertext is corrupt (e.g. env-key rotation, or legacy plaintext test seed) the InvalidToken bubbles up as a 500 on ANY Twilio webhook hit. Wrap in try/except and return None so `_load_ctx` returns None → graceful 'This number is not configured' TwiML instead of a stacktrace + 500 to Twilio.

invitations.remove_member compares `user_id == user.get('id')` and queries `db.users.find_one({'id': user_id, ...})`, but the users collection uses `user_id` (not `id`) as its primary key. Owner-initiated member deletion of a real teammate will always 404. (Non-owner 403 guard fires before this, so the 403 test still passes.) Rename to `user_id` in both places.

PhoneSms.jsx: the review request says 'Provision button is disabled' should be visible, but my selector `button:has-text("Provision")` returned 0 hits. Please verify — either the button was conditionally not rendered when Twilio isn't connected, or wording differs. Low priority; the amber connect-Twilio banner IS shown.
critical_code_review_comments: sms_compliance.py record_consent_transition — Mongo ObjectId leak into HTTP response (FIXED here).

credentials_service.set_twilio validates by fetching account via API-Key auth, but doesn't guard against a client claiming an account_sid that belongs to a different Twilio account than the API-Key. Twilio's Client(api_key_sid, api_key_secret, account_sid) allows any account_sid string in the constructor — the fetch will 401 if wrong, so validation is functionally OK, but consider explicitly asserting `acct.sid == req.account_sid`.

email_service Resend validation calls GET /domains — that's a scoped resource and can return 401 for API keys that are actually valid but limited-scope. Consider GET /api-keys or a dummy send with 'dry-run'. Not blocking.
twilio_service.sms_inbound STOP handler records opt_out for BOTH care and marketing — good. START only opts back into 'care', not marketing — appropriate per marketing-consent-must-be-explicit rule.

billing_cycle.record_overage_for_clinic is idempotent per (clinic_id, period) via overage_records upsert — good. However /close returns 200 with per-clinic errors embedded in results[i].error — an admin cron observer might miss failures. Consider adding a top-level 'errors_count' field.

rca of the issue: One backend bug found and fixed: sms_compliance.record_consent_transition returned the inserted event doc still carrying Mongo ObjectId (`_id`), which FastAPI cannot JSON-serialise. The `opt_in` and `opt_out` HTTP routes returned this doc directly, causing 500 Internal Server Error on every call. Reproduction: POST /api/compliance/sms/consent {phone_e164:'+15551110001', consent_type:'care', source:'x', disclosure_version:'v1'} → 500 with ValueError [TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable")]. Mitigation: added `doc.pop('_id', None)` after `await db.consent_events.insert_one(doc)`. Now returns clean JSON. Confirmed by re-running the full test suite: 22/22 pass.
